headline: COPPER BOUNCES FROM BEAR MARKET LOW AS CHINA SCRAMBLES FOR METAL — Record Yangshan Premiums Signal Physical Demand Intact
snippet: Copper prices bounced from bear market lows on November 22 as the market absorbed evidence of intense Chinese demand for physical copper even as LME three-month contracts briefly touched $11,994/t — their lowest level since late March 2026 — during the prior week. Comex December copper hit as low as $5.4405/lb before recovering, in a session where the fundamental disconnect between financial market selling and Chinese physical demand continued to widen: Yangshan import premiums remain near their all-time record of $500/t recorded earlier this week, with Chinese buyers prepared to pay extraordinary premiums to secure copper deliveries even as leveraged funds drive paper prices lower. Tens of thousands of tonnes of US copper continue to be rerouted to China via January deliveries as sellers arbitrage the premium. For junior copper investors, the bounce confirms that the November bear market remains primarily a financial-market event rather than a demand-destruction event — the question now is whether the technical bounce holds above the $12,000/t LME threshold or whether a retest of lows follows before physical buying fully reasserts.

headline: ASX 200 MINERS SMASHED IN WEEK 47 ROUT — PLS TUMBLES 8.4% TO A$2.62, Copper Falls 10% To 7-Month Low As AI Deleveraging Extends Into Hard Rock Stocks
snippet: Australian mining shares absorbed another severe beating in week 47 of 2026, with Pilbara Minerals (ASX: PLS) falling 8.39% to A$2.62 — emblematic of the broader damage across the ASX 200's hard-rock resource sector as copper tumbled 10% to a 7-month low of approximately US$5.50/lb and AI-driven deleveraging that began in US equities continued to sweep through global commodity markets. The sell-off reflects the same dynamics driving the TSX-V's fifth consecutive weekly loss: algorithmic selling in US markets cascading into global mining equity indices, with Australian-listed lithium, copper, and iron ore names bearing the brunt given their ASX liquidity. For retail investors watching the Australian junior mining market as a proxy for TSX-V sentiment, the PLS fall is significant: Pilbara Minerals is one of the most liquid pure-play lithium names on any exchange, and its 8.4% single-week loss signals the depth of capitulation still occurring in battery metals. The coming week will test whether Thanksgiving-thinned US markets allow some stabilization, or whether the rout extends into the final week of November.

headline: FREEPORT PAYS C$110M FOR 51% OF TDG GOLD'S AURORA WEST IN BC — Copper Giant Doubles Down On Toodoggone District As Junior Copper Stocks Sell Off
snippet: Freeport-McMoRan agreed to pay C$110 million in cash for an initial 51% stake in TDG Gold's Aurora West copper-gold project in British Columbia's Toodoggone district — one of the most significant major-company investments in a BC copper development project during 2026's junior mining correction. Under the binding joint venture agreement, Freeport can increase its interest to 75% by spending a further C$80 million on exploration and paying TDG an additional C$40 million. TDG retains its Shasta and Baker properties, and Amarc Resources holds participation rights in some Aurora West claims through its Joy joint venture. For TSX-V junior copper investors, the Freeport deal is a significant validation signal: the world's largest publicly traded copper producer is deploying C$110 million into a BC porphyry copper development asset at precisely the moment when junior copper equities are trading at multi-year lows — a pattern of major-company strategic buying during equity corrections that has historically preceded sharp re-ratings for nearby exploration companies in the same district.

headline: ALTIUS MINERALS ACQUIRES TNR GOLD ROYALTY PORTFOLIO FOR C$122M — Los Azules Copper And Mariana Lithium NSRs The Strategic Prize; Shotgun Gold Spun Out
snippet: Altius Minerals agreed to acquire all outstanding shares of TNR Gold (TSXV: TNR) for approximately C$122 million in an all-share deal, gaining royalty exposure to McEwen Copper's Los Azules copper-gold porphyry in Argentina (effective 0.36% NSR) and the Mariana lithium project (effective 1.35% NSR), alongside several other royalty interests. TNR shareholders receive 0.0072 Altius shares plus 0.25 shares of a new SpinCo for each TNR share — equivalent to roughly C$0.48 per share, a ~60% premium to TNR's pre-announcement close — with activist Eucalyptus backing the deal. SpinCo holds the Shotgun gold project in Alaska, with Altius retaining a 0.5% NSR on that asset. A shareholder meeting is scheduled for December 8, with closing targeted Q1 2027. For royalty-focused retail investors, Altius paying a 60% premium for NSR positions on two major South American critical metal developments — during a period of commodity equity weakness — signals that high-quality development-stage royalties on world-class projects command significant strategic premiums regardless of near-term metal price volatility.

headline: WHY GOLD MINING STOCKS FALL 50% HARDER THAN GOLD IN CORRECTIONS — Beta, Leverage, And Cost Inflation Explain Junior Miner Underperformance
snippet: Discovery Alert's November analysis examines why gold mining stocks — including TSX-V juniors — consistently fall harder and faster than gold during corrections, explaining the situation where producers and developers have underperformed gold's physical price by 30-50% during 2026's sell-off. The analysis identifies three key amplifiers: operating leverage (a 10% fall in gold price can destroy 30-50% of a producer's earnings in a high-cost environment), financial leverage (companies carrying debt see equity value collapse faster than the enterprise value), and cost inflation that has permanently raised breakeven prices for many gold operations during 2025-2026, narrowing margins even at apparently elevated gold prices. For self-directed junior mining investors frustrated by their TSX-V gold positions underperforming spot gold, this analysis frames the underperformance not as irrational but as mathematically expected given leverage — and argues that the same leverage works in reverse on the way up, historically delivering 2-5x gold's percentage gain during recoveries from oversold conditions.

headline: NORWAY'S BATTERY MINERAL WEALTH IS REAL BUT REMAINS UNDEFINED — Nickel, Cobalt, Vanadium Deposits Need More Drilling Before Development Case Is Made
snippet: Discovery Alert's November analysis profiles Norway's emerging battery minerals sector — covering nickel, cobalt, and vanadium — in the context of Europe's growing push for domestic critical mineral supply chains. Norway's geology hosts ultramafic sequences with historical nickel-cobalt occurrences, but unlike Sweden's Bergslagen tungsten district or Finland's nickel belt, most Norwegian battery mineral projects remain at early-stage geophysical survey and mapping phases, with limited modern drill data to define resource-grade geology. The analysis frames Norway's challenge as one of translating geologically credible prospectivity into defined deposit inventory — the same gap that makes early-stage critical mineral exploration in Scandinavia a higher-risk, higher-optionality bet compared to more advanced Canadian or Australian jurisdiction peers. Norway's mining regime is favorable and improving, its permitting timeline is competitive within the EU, and its resource potential is real — but investors need to distinguish between companies with actual drill-defined resources and those offering prospectivity stories backed primarily by historical surveys.

headline: POLICY NOW DRIVES THE BATTERY MATERIALS OUTLOOK TO 2035 — IRA, CBAM, And Critical Mineral Deals Rewriting Which Deposits Get Built And Which Get Stranded
snippet: Discovery Alert's November analysis argues that the battery materials investment thesis through 2035 is now dominated by policy frameworks rather than commodity prices alone — with the US Inflation Reduction Act's domestic content requirements, the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, and bilateral critical minerals deals between allied nations determining which new mines can access premium-priced supply contracts and which must compete on cost alone with Chinese producers. Three tiers of battery mineral projects are emerging: Tier 1 in IRA-qualifying jurisdictions (US, Canada, Australia, FTA partners) accessing US EV supply chain premium pricing; Tier 2 in friendly-but-non-qualifying nations (EU member states, Japan, South Korea) benefiting from CBAM and domestic procurement preferences; and Tier 3 in non-aligned jurisdictions competing head-to-head with low-cost Chinese supply. For TSX-V investors, the analysis makes the case that jurisdiction is becoming as important as grade and tonnage in determining a battery mineral project's terminal value — a framework that significantly enhances the premium for well-permitted Canadian and Australian assets regardless of near-term spot price noise.

headline: MOTLEY FOOL: 3 CRITICAL MINERAL STOCKS THAT COULD MAKE YOU A FORTUNE BY 2035 — Rare Earths, Copper, And Lithium Developers Flagged For Long-Term Retail Investors
snippet: The Motley Fool's November 19 analysis identifies three critical mineral stocks positioned for multi-year outperformance as the energy transition and strategic resource competition drive structural demand above historical trend for rare earths, copper, and lithium. The piece frames the current broad correction in critical mineral equities as a potential entry window for long-horizon retail investors: the structural supply-demand case for each metal — driven by EV adoption, grid storage buildout, and defence-sector demand — has not changed, while equity prices have compressed sharply from 2026 highs. The analysis applies a framework separating 'resource reality' (deposit size, grade, metallurgy) from 'policy tailwind' (IRA eligibility, strategic alliance exposure) to rank near-term development probability. For TSX-V and ASX investors already holding junior miners in the same sectors, mainstream framing of the 2035 thesis is a useful sentiment signal: companies that feature prominently in retail investor media tend to attract the first waves of retail capital when sentiment turns, and knowing which names are on that shortlist helps position ahead of the recovery.

headline: MACROPLANE: THE COMPLETE RARE EARTH INVESTOR GUIDE FOR NOVEMBER 2026 — Volatility Drivers, Supply Chain Risk, And Entry Point Framework Analyzed
snippet: Macroplane's comprehensive November 2026 rare earth investor guide synthesizes the month's major sector events — China's export policy uncertainty post-November 10 pause expiry, USA Rare Earth's post-earnings selloff and partial recovery, Critical Metals' 28.7% dilution-driven plunge, and rising Pr-Nd oxide prices in China — into a framework for retail investors navigating one of the most volatile critical metals sectors. The guide examines the fundamental tension in rare earth equity investing: the structural demand story (permanent magnets for EVs and wind turbines requiring Pr-Nd oxide) is intact and strengthening, while equity prices are dominated by policy headlines, company-specific balance sheet events, and macro de-risking. For self-directed investors building rare earth exposure, the guide provides specific entry-point criteria: quality of domestic processing infrastructure, feedstock security beyond Chinese-controlled sources, magnet plant operational status, and cash runway to survive the current equity correction. The November data showing Pr-Nd oxide prices in China rising even as Western rare earth equities sold off — a physical-equity divergence — is flagged as a historically reliable precursor to sector re-rating.

headline: SPROTT: GOLD AND SILVER DEMAND HOLDS FIRM AS PERFECT STORM RAGES — ETF Inflows Turn Positive, Central Banks On Track To Beat 2025 Purchase Record
snippet: Sprott Asset Management's November 2026 precious metals commentary argues that physical gold and silver demand is proving resilient beneath the financial market turbulence, with ETF inflows turning modestly positive for the first time in eight consecutive weeks and global central bank purchases tracking ahead of 2025's record level. Despite gold trading near 2026 lows — down approximately 36% from January's $5,588 all-time high — the demand picture from institutional buyers and central banks has not deteriorated in a manner consistent with a structurally broken bull market. Sprott highlights the gold/silver ratio near 79 as a signal that silver is anomalously cheap relative to gold — a condition that has historically resolved through silver outperforming on recoveries. The report frames the November correction as a forced liquidation event within a larger intact bull trend, distinguishing between the financial conditions that caused the correction (rate hike expectations, dollar strength, algorithmic deleveraging) and the structural factors that drive gold's long-term bull case (central bank diversification away from US dollar reserves, geopolitical uncertainty premium, and sovereign debt sustainability concerns).
